Speaking in Paris, Jensen Huang said Nvidia expects to unveil $2 billion in new European AI deals within a week, on top of $8 billion deployed there over the past year.
Nvidia also took stakes in four French startups and pledged $250 million in compute for UK AI safety research.

slides.headline: Jensen Huang is on a European spending spree: *$2 billion* in new AI deals

slides.heading: *$2 billion* more for Europe
paras: Speaking in Paris on Tuesday, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the chipmaker expects to unveil $2 billion in European AI deals within the next week.
That comes on top of the $8 billion Nvidia has already deployed across Europe over the past year. His tour also includes London and Berlin.

slides.heading: Four *French bets*
paras: In Paris, Nvidia took minority stakes in four French startups: robotics maker Genesis AI, planning software firm Pigment, materials discovery startup Entalpic and health platform Doctolib.
Financial terms were not disclosed. Nvidia also committed to helping Doctolib train its AI models.

slides.heading: *$250 million* for UK safety
paras: On Wednesday, Nvidia pledged $250 million in computing power over five years, about $50 million a year, for UK research on agentic AI safety and security.
Oxford's BOLD lab, UCL's SOFAIR lab and Imperial College London get dedicated support. The compute will come through UK-based Nvidia cloud partners.

slides.heading: Capability *and* safety
paras: "AI capability and safety must advance together," Huang said. The research will focus on secure agents, open-model security and real-world threat mitigation.

paras.t: UK AI Minister Kanishka Narayan called it "a vote of confidence in our world-leading strength and expertise in AI research."

slides.hook: Huang says more European deals land within a week. Follow to see where Nvidia's money goes next.
